facts.text: You play the T side on Inferno.
The bomb has not been planted; about 35 s remain on the round clock.
The bomb is on the ground in Top of Mid.
Your team is positioned: 2 in Middle.
The positions of two defenders are unknown.
The defenders have lost 2 rounds in a row, so they are likely on a reduced buy. Basis: public scoreboard: CT lost recent rounds of this half.

Keep the default and take information first

Play slowly and listen for rotations

responses.label: Adjust the plan to the new information

debrief.whyItWorks: With limited clock, taking space with utility while the defence is unsettled is the most reliable way to plant in time. Here, 2 players faced 2 with about 35 seconds left.
debrief.cost: It spends the team's utility and options at once, leaving little for the post-plant.
debrief.assumption: The defenders cannot rotate enough players to the site before the plant.
debrief.breaksWhen: The defence stacks the chosen site and has its own utility ready for the execute.

evidenceReview.explanation: The utility left sets how much of the plan can be forced rather than hoped for. Here the team held 1 utility item.
The round clock bounds how long any plan can take. Here the round clock stood near 35 seconds.
The head count sets how many duels the team can lose and still carry out its plan. Here it was 2 against 2.

debrief.followupReview: The proposed best answer to the new information was: Adjust the plan to the new information. Reasoning: the new information shows where an opponent is or what utility they have used, so adapting the plan is worth more than repeating it.
debrief.strongestAlternative: The closest alternative was to gather information before acting, spending clock to reduce the guess.

counterfactual.changedFact: The defenders are known to have stacked the target site.
counterfactual.effect: The execute meets a full defence, and taking information or faking becomes stronger.
